question_text: Distinguish between speed and velocity.
answer_text: Speed is the distance travelled by an object in a given interval of time. Velocity is the displacement of an object in a given interval of time. Speed = distance / time; Velocity = displacement / time. Speed is scalar quantity i.e. it has only magnitude. Velocity is vector quantity i.e. it has both magnitude as well as direction.
final_answer: Thus, speed is a scalar quantity while velocity is a vector quantity.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of basic definitions and differences between speed and velocity.

question_text: When will you say a body is in (i) uniform acceleration? (ii) non-uniform acceleration?
answer_text: (i) A body is said to be in uniform acceleration if it travels in a straight line and its velocity increases or decreases by equal amounts in equal intervals of time. (ii) A body is said to be in non-uniform acceleration if the rate of change of its velocity is not constant.
final_answer: Thus, uniform acceleration involves constant change in velocity, while non-uniform does not.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of definitions and examples of acceleration types.
